title: EOD: Enabling Low Latency GNN Inference via Near-Memory Concatenate Aggregation
problem: Real-time GNN inference for online services requires an inductive setup where the system must first prepare the computational graph and node features before executing inference, with this preparation step dominating end-to-end latency. The neighborhood explosion problem causes exponential growth in memory access and computation as the number of GNN layers increases.
motivation: Graph-database-backed online services increasingly require low-latency per-request GNN inference, but the heavy host-memory access and data I/O in the preparation step, combined with neighborhood explosion, make sub-millisecond targets unachievable on conventional systems.
method: EOD co-designs algorithm and hardware to tackle both challenges. On the algorithmic side, it introduces a precomputation method for training nodes that converts exponential neighborhood aggregation to linear complexity, and a concatenated Zero-Value Compression (ZVC) scheme to compact the stored precomputed hidden features. On the hardware side, EOD implements a Near-Memory Processing (NMP) architecture that performs aggregation directly on ZVC-compressed, concatenated feature data without decompressing to host memory, exploiting the high internal memory bandwidth to eliminate the PCIe/host-memory bottleneck during the preparation stage.
key_novelty: A concatenated ZVC compression format co-designed with a dedicated NMP aggregation engine that operates natively on compressed GNN features, eliminating the host-side memory access bottleneck entirely.
contributions: A precomputation algorithm that reduces GNN neighborhood aggregation complexity from exponential to linear for inductive inference settings.
A concatenated ZVC compression method that minimizes storage overhead for precomputed hidden features.
An NMP architecture that performs efficient aggregation directly on concatenated ZVC-compressed data in host memory.
End-to-end latency speedups of 17.9x geomean (up to 74.3x) over GPU baseline and 981x geomean over existing NMP aggregation architectures.

metrics.speedup: 981.1x geomean aggregation speedup over baseline; 17.9x geomean end-to-end speedup over GPU baseline; up to 74.3x end-to-end speedup

baselines: existing NMP architecture for GNN aggregation
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation covers the preparation/aggregation phase but full end-to-end system integration details (e.g., host CPU interaction, scalability to very large graphs) are not elaborated in the abstract.
primary_theme: Near-memory GNN aggregation with compressed feature precomputation
